question: How did 'monetized in 7-10 days' channels actually qualify?

official_rules.source: YouTube Help 72851 (opened 2026-11-04) and, for the early-access tier, a search snippet of YouTube Help 13429240 (not opened)
full_ads_tier: 1,000 subscribers + 4,000 public watch hours in 12 months
1,000 subscribers + 10 million public Shorts views in 90 days
official_rules.shorts_feed_hours: watch hours from Shorts-feed views do NOT count toward the 4,000 hours (YouTube Help 72851)
official_rules.early_access_tier: 500 subscribers + 3 public uploads in 90 d + 3M Shorts views in 90 d or 3,000 watch hours in 12 m: fan funding and shopping only, NOT ad revenue (search snippet, not opened)
official_rules.reported_2027_change: vidIQ blog (not confirmed on YouTube's own page as fetched): from 2027-02-01 the full tier doubles (8,000 h or 20M Shorts views). YouTube Help only says the updated terms start 2027-02-01.

cases.label: E'Calm - 'The YouTube Shorts System That Got Me Monetized in 7 Days'
cases.format: Shorts, edited in CapCut (captions, overlays, scoreboard)
cases.claim: channel created 2026-02-10, monetized 'in the same February', $3,700 in 28 days, $7,700 in 90 days
what_does_not_add_up: the title says 7 days, the transcript says 'monetized in the same February' (up to ~18 days), and the video is three months later
he says the account is 5 YEARS old and that 'you should use an old account / warm it up': it is not a new channel
10M Shorts views in <=18 days would need ~550K views/day; he says each video gets '40K+' views
no subscriber or watch-hour counter is shown
cases.reading: INFERENCE: either the old account already had subscribers/hours/views history, or the early-access tier was counted as 'monetized'. Not verifiable.
cases.risk: re-uploading TikTok clips is the 'reused/inauthentic content' risk YouTube enforces; he says so himself. Sells courses (Gumroad), a vidIQ affiliate link, a '$400K system' upsell. HYPE + COURSE.

cases.label: AI Cash Tom - 'This Skeleton Channel Got Monetized in 7 Days'
cases.niche: AI skeleton Shorts ('What if you tried X for 1 year?')
cases.format: Shorts, 9:16, AI images -> AI video clips -> ElevenLabs voice -> CapCut
cases.claim: 'channels like Skelly Skills pulled 21 million views with only 28 videos in 1 month'
cases.route_stated: Shorts path implied (21M views in a month would exceed 10M)
what_does_not_add_up: the 7-day claim is about a DIFFERENT channel whose analytics are not shown
I found no independent source for '21M views / 28 videos / 1 month' (a web search returned other skeleton channels only)
no subscriber number, no monetization proof
cases.reading: UNVERIFIED. If true it is the Shorts-views route with a viral format, not hours.
cases.useful_structure: title = first spoken line; 'generate 10-s clips and use the best 2-3 s'; hook uses the wildest motion first; month-by-month escalation with jokes; captions 1-2 words. HYPE (962 views, free prompt doc as lead magnet).

cases.evidence: metadata and chapter titles only (transcript not read)
cases.reading: chapter titles point to compilations of existing videos; unverified; 2 years old

cases.label: Medium - 'I MONETIZED a YouTube Channel In 7 Days'
'I MONETIZED A Youtube Channel In 5/8 Days Only To Prove It's NOT Luck'
Gumroad/Payhip pages ('monetized in 7 days', 'already monetized')
cases.reading: sales pages; one sells pre-monetized channels (marketing, unverified)

verdict: No verifiable case found of a brand-new channel reaching 1,000 subs + 4,000 public long hours in 7-10 days. Hours need ~240,000 viewed minutes inside 12 months.

The only mechanically plausible fast routes are (a) 10M Shorts views in 90 days after a viral hit (about 555K views/day if done in 18 days), (b) an aged or pre-existing channel with history, (c) 'monetized' meaning the 500-subscriber early-access tier (fan funding only), (d) buying a pre-monetized channel. Which one each creator used is NOT shown in the sources read.
Every case read is a course/lead-magnet seller; two are 'YouTube Shorts' with reused or templated clips. Treat as hype for planning.
Transferable (structure only): the first spoken line equals the title; the strongest motion first; one-idea escalating script. These match the Bible Shorts winners, not a monetization shortcut.
